spatial_claims.claim: Produce AB beyond B and cut off BC equal to x, creating collinear arrangement A-B-C with B between A and C
AB > BC (i.e., AB is the greater term of the binomial AC), since a > b implies AB > x = BC

configuration_map: The entire geometric configuration is a single line with three collinear points: A---B---C. AB is the assigned rational straight line and serves as the greater term. BC is a segment equal to x (the fourth proportional), placed on the extension of AB beyond B, serving as the lesser term. AC = AB + BC is the resulting binomial straight line. No auxiliary points, triangles, circles, or angles are constructed. All substantive reasoning is algebraic, concerning commensurability relations, proportions, and the definition of a fourth binomial.
pass_reason: The proof is overwhelmingly algebraic, dealing with commensurability and proportion relations. The only spatial claim is the trivial collinear construction A-B-C on a line, which is self-consistent. No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior point claims, no ray orderings, and no circle arguments appear. There are no complex geometric configurations that could harbor contradictions.
